episode.title: Ep. 181 — Al Qaeda’s leader has a new rallying cry. We should listen.

persons.name: Saif al-Adel
persons.role: De facto (still unofficial) leader of al-Qaeda after Zawahiri's death; sheltering in Iran; wrote pseudonymous As-Sahab article calling for migration to Afghanistan to train for attacks on the West and 'the Zionists'

mentions.quote: you had the head of Al-Qaeda, Saif al-Adel. Well, Al-Qaeda hasn't officially named him after the death of Ayman al-Zawahiri... their next leader is sheltering in Iran

under a pseudonym writes an article for a publication that was put out by As-Sahab... he calls for people across the globe for westerners and others to migrate to Afghanistan to gain experience to conduct attacks against the West and... the Zionists

persons.name: Ayman al-Zawahiri
persons.status_detail: killed at a safe house in Kabul by the US in July 2022; death never admitted by al-Qaeda or confirmed by the Taliban

mentions.quote: The al-Qaeda never admitted he was killed in Kabul and the Taliban never confirmed it as well.
his people also sheltered Ayman al-Zawahiri when he was killed at a safe house in July 22 by the U.S.

persons.name: Sirajuddin Haqqani
persons.role: Taliban interior minister, one of two Taliban deputy emirs, head of the Haqqani Network; Specially Designated Global Terrorist with $10M FBI reward

mentions.quote: I was shocked when I saw that Haqqani was in the UAE, right, meeting with the UAE president. I think it was June 5th.
Sirajuddin Haqqani, you know, FBI, $10 million reward, the blood of thousands of Americans... Haqqani associated Twitter accounts were live streaming him at the Hajj in Saudi Arabia
Siraj is also the interior minister for the Taliban's Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan... and also one of the two deputy emirs for the Taliban
Nothing gets done in Afghanistan without Siraj Haqqani being involved.
Haqqani is the one... he's closest to Pakistani ISI... closest to al-Qaeda as well. He's the nexus. He is the most dangerous.
he describes him as the Taliban Shogun

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Founder of the Haqqani Network; father of Sirajuddin

mentions.quote: His Haqqani network, which he runs, established by his father, Jalaluddin Haqqani, is a foreign terrorist organization.
Siraj and his father were the ones that put the band back together

persons.name: Anas Haqqani
persons.role: Senior Haqqani Network / Taliban figure; brother of Sirajuddin; performed Hajj with him June 2024

mentions.quote: His brother was there, Anas, the deputy minister of defense was there, the former shadow governor of Helmand was there.

persons.name: Haji Mali Khan
persons.role: Senior Haqqani Network figure; Roggio names him as a possible successor to Sirajuddin within the network

mentions.quote: If we killed him tomorrow, I suspect there's someone within his organization, you know, Haji Mali Khan, or there's others

persons.name: Hibatullah Akhundzada
persons.role: Emir of the Taliban; reclusive; former jurisprudence leader in the Taliban shura

mentions.quote: the current Emir of the Taliban, Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada, is also sort of reclusive... Hibatullah Akhundzada was the jurisprudence leader, you know, in the Taliban Shura

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Founding emir of the Taliban; reclusive; his death was concealed by the Taliban, causing a near-breakup

mentions.quote: when the Taliban had their little almost breakup over the scandal of them playing Weekend at Bernie's with the corpse of Mullah Omar, Siraj and his father were the ones that put the band back together

persons.name: Mullah Yaqoob
persons.role: Taliban defense minister; one of the three biggest Taliban players per hosts; not designated

mentions.quote: I don't know if Yaqoob has done it either. Because that means he's the only one of the three, who I consider some of the bigger players, to have done that.
Yaqoob isn't designated to my knowledge.

persons.name: Ahmad Massoud
aliases: the son of the lion of Panjshir
persons.role: Head of the National Resistance Front; son of Ahmad Shah Massoud

mentions.quote: look at the son of the lion of Panjshir, right, his performance versus Sirajuddin Haqqani... the current head of the National Resistance Front... one is a question mark that has to earn leadership

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Massoud
persons.role: Late Northern Alliance commander (referenced as Ahmad Massoud's father)

mentions.quote: the son of the lion of Panjshir

persons.name: Sami Sadat

mentions.quote: General Sami Sadat, former top-notch Afghan general. I had the pleasure of testifying alongside him in Congress.

persons.role: Guest co-host; retired USAF Middle East Foreign Area Officer, military affairs fellow at The Bulwark, Long War Journal contributor

mentions.quote: Will is a retired Middle East Foreign Affairs Officer. He's also the military affairs fellow at the Bulwark.

persons.name: Barnett Rubin
persons.role: Academic/former Obama-era official involved in Doha outreach; wrote that Sirajuddin Haqqani 'no longer poses a threat to Americans'

mentions.quote: Barnett Rubin... comes out in an article and tells us, Sirajuddin Haqqani, quote, no longer poses a threat to Americans, end quote.

persons.name: Joe Biden
persons.role: US President; withdrew from Afghanistan; implied partnering with the Taliban against ISKP

mentions.quote: President Biden has said as much in different press conferences. He didn't say, we are working with the Taliban to defeat the Islamic State. But... he basically implied that.

persons.role: President of the UAE; met Sirajuddin Haqqani in Abu Dhabi, ~5 Jun 2024

events.description: Saif al-Adel, under a pseudonym, publishes an As-Sahab article calling on Westerners and others to migrate to Afghanistan to train with the Taliban/Haqqanis and attack the West and 'the Zionists'.
Sirajuddin Haqqani visits the UAE and meets the UAE president in Abu Dhabi.
Haqqani-linked accounts livestream Sirajuddin Haqqani performing Hajj in Saudi Arabia with Anas Haqqani, the deputy defense minister, the former Helmand shadow governor and other Taliban figures.
US kills Zawahiri at a Haqqani-sheltered safe house in Kabul; al-Qaeda never admitted it, Taliban never confirmed.
Barnett Rubin article claims Sirajuddin Haqqani 'no longer poses a threat to Americans'.
Taliban ministers travel to Russia for conferences.
UN Monitoring Team reports al-Qaeda training camps in 10 of 34 Afghan provinces, madrassas in 5, safe houses in 4, a media center and a weapons depot in Panjshir.
US military issues its first reward ($75,000) for Sirajuddin Haqqani.
Taliban conceals Mullah Omar's death ('Weekend at Bernie's'), nearly splitting the movement; Siraj and Jalaluddin Haqqani reunite it.
Doha agreement legitimized the Taliban and restricted Afghan offensive operations, demoralizing Afghan forces.
Al-Qaeda in Iraq seizes Barwana and Haditha for ~12 hours, executing police chief.
Al-Qaeda bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, preceded by two declarations of war in the 1990s.
Another Doha conference on Afghanistan planned, which hosts criticize.

key_claims: Saif al-Adel's call to migrate to Afghanistan for training is a credible threat because al-Qaeda has Taliban state sponsorship and infrastructure (camps in 10 provinces, Panjshir depot).
Al-Qaeda never left Afghanistan; the 'resurgence' framing was cover for withdrawal.
Al-Qaeda has not acknowledged Zawahiri's death because its successor shelters in Iran, and the Taliban has not confirmed it because it denies al-Qaeda's presence.

Sirajuddin Haqqani is the nexus between the Taliban, al-Qaeda and Pakistan's ISI and the most influential Taliban leader; hosts debate whether he will become emir or prefers wielding power as 'Taliban Shogun'.
Siraj's UAE visit and livestreamed Hajj (June 2024) show Taliban/al-Qaeda confidence and a rehabilitation tour toward international recognition.
Taliban internal disputes are squabbles within a party, not factional splits; the interim government is stable.
Partnering with the Taliban against ISKP is a mistake; Taliban-IS enmity is practical, not ideological.
